items.text: Copy-paste bug: the second `requireNonNull` checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` will be silently accepted and likely cause a NullPointerException later when it's used.
A prefix shorter than 5 chars throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false in isAccessTokenId matcher
AccessTokenContext's constructor calls requireNonNull(grantType) twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId which can produce malformed encoded IDs or downstream NPEs
V1/legacy token exchange in AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:410 doesn't set grant type, causing 'na' instead of proper grant shortcut
Factory builds HashMaps for 3- and 4-value enums (SessionType, TokenType) where an enum static fromShortcut would do
AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken reads the requesting client rather than the token's client
Line 73 repeats the grantType null-check instead of checking rawTokenId, so rawTokenId == null can slip through and later be encoded as '...:null' instead of failing fast

client_credentials tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of the registered 'cc', because this grant builds tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context
The isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the grant type shortcut with substring(3, 5) but the encoding format places it at positions 4-5 (should be substring(4, 6))

Copy-paste slip: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and a null raw id encodes to e.g. 'onrtac:null'

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
Label 'area/dependencies' could not be found and needs to be created before Dependabot can use it
Test catches RuntimeException instead of the specific parsing exception, making the test pass on unrelated failures like IndexOutOfBoundsException or NullPointerException
isAccessTokenId() has inverted logic where equals(expectedGrantShortcut) branch returns false when it matches, causing it to reject correct tokens and accept wrong grant shortcuts
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) is used without checking for a missing provider, which will cause NPE during token issuance if the SPI isn't available/registered
grantType field is captured once in constructor but setFormParams() can replace parameters later without updating it, making getGrantType() return stale data
isAccessTokenId() may throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for short prefixes instead of returning false
The isAccessTokenId matcher condition is inverted - it returns false when the grant matches instead of when it doesn't
Make `getShortcut()` a default SPI method; adding it as abstract breaks existing custom grant factories on upgrade.
UMA / permission-grant tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of 'pg' because the path never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE
isAccessTokenId() validates grant shortcut incorrectly: substring(3, 5) doesn't match the described 'grant is last 2 chars of the 6-char prefix'
Context.grantType is captured from formParams at construction and not refreshed by setFormParams
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic - returns false when grant shortcut matches instead of when they do not match

Token ID decoding hard-requires a 6-character context prefix (2+2+2), but OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc suggests 3-letter shortcuts with no validation ensuring shortcuts are 2 characters, causing custom grants with 3-letter shortcuts to generate IDs that the decoder rejects
New unit test uses org.junit.Assert.assertEquals with actual and expected swapped, against docs/tests-development.md guidance; failure messages would read backwards
Outdated comment 'starts at 4th char' left over from earlier 3-letter encoding
UMA/permission grant ('pg') is never emitted because AuthorizationTokenService.java:358 doesn't set the grant type
Commit format breaches CONTRIBUTING.md: two commits instead of one, ee2491268a uses lowercase 'closes #37118', daffb05b5a has no issue link

isAccessTokenId matcher reads the wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)) and its comparison is inverted (returns false on equality), so it accepts essentially any grant; the updated expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions never verify the grant shortcut
grantsToShortcuts duplicates sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, gt) with a hand-maintained, unsynchronised cache that can go stale on undeploy
The lazy refresh paths at Lines 106-137 bypass the one-time duplicate check, allowing a custom grant to overwrite an existing shortcut mapping at runtime
The hot-deploy refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut adds entries without the duplicate-shortcut check postInit performs
User-visible change to access-token jti and event token_id format (bare UUID -> '<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>') has no upgrade/release note, breaching PR-CHECKLIST.md

AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken is now invoked for every access token, dereferencing session.getContext().getClient(); a context without a client would NPE even when no mappers run
Client-credentials access tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of 'cc' because ClientCredentialsGrantType never calls createTokenResponse or sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
@Column(name='ID', length = 36) annotation is now shorter than the new 43-char access-token ids (stale annotation)
Label 'area/ci' could not be found and needs to be created before Dependabot can use it
The maps include UNKNOWN 'un' shortcuts so decode accepts 'ununna:x' which encodeTokenId refuses to encode, causing asymmetry
isAccessTokenId matcher reads substring(3,5) but the grant shortcut is at position [4,6) (session 2 + token type 2 + grant 2), causing incorrect offset
The new access-token matcher rejects valid grant shortcuts because it reads the wrong substring and returns false on a match.
Public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed from the grant SPI, breaking API compatibility
V1 (legacy), federated and impersonation token-exchange tokens are encoded with grant 'na' because they never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE
Copy-paste slip: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, leaving rawTokenId unchecked and encoding null as '<prefix>:null'

Javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', but decoding requires the prefix to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2); a 3-letter shortcut encodes fine but produces IDs getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects with IllegalArgumentException
isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring indices - substring(3, 5) extracts characters at indices 3-4 ('ta') instead of the grant type which should be substring(4, 6)
OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning null from getShortcut() causes NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put
New abstract getShortcut() method has no default, causing AbstractMethodError for custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against old interface

Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") is a typo that validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, allowing null raw ID to slip through and potentially cause malformed encoded token IDs or later failures

Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias; the patch uses both names inconsistently (OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, grants/TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE)
The decoder assumes a fixed 2+2+2 prefix but the factory never validates that grant shortcuts are exactly 2 characters, meaning custom grants can emit token IDs that later fail to decode
isAccessTokenId matcher condition is inverted: returns false when value equals expected shortcut instead of true, making grant-type checks ineffective
In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

getShortcut() is a new abstract method with no default; a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface throws AbstractMethodError in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit at server startup
A null shortcut from getShortcut() causes NPE on ConcurrentHashMap.put in postInit
isAccessTokenId matcher throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for prefixes shorter than 5 characters instead of returning false

issues.claim: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the requireNonNull call with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and gets encoded as '<prefix>:null', or causes a later NPE.
The isAccessTokenId matcher throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for prefixes shorter than 5 characters instead of returning false.
The isAccessTokenId matcher extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3, 5). The grant shortcut sits at positions 4-5 of the 2+2+2 prefix, so the correct call is substring(4, 6).
The isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic: it returns false when the extracted value equals the expected grant shortcut, so it rejects correct tokens and accepts wrong grant shortcuts.
V1/legacy, federated and impersonation token-exchange tokens are encoded with grant 'na' because these paths never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE (AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:410).

Client-credentials access tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of 'cc'. ClientCredentialsGrantType builds tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken() and never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the client session context.
UMA/permission-grant tokens are encoded with grant 'na' instead of 'pg' because AuthorizationTokenService.java:358 never sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE.
The factory builds HashMaps for the 3- and 4-value enums SessionType and TokenType, where a static fromShortcut method on the enum would do.
AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken reads the requesting client rather than the token's client.

AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken is now invoked for every access token and dereferences session.getContext().getClient(). A context without a client causes an NPE even when no mappers run.
The Dependabot label 'area/dependencies' does not exist.
The Dependabot label 'area/ci' does not exist.

The test catches generic RuntimeException instead of the specific IllegalArgumentException thrown by the parser, so it also passes on unrelated failures such as IndexOutOfBoundsException or NullPointerException.
session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) is used without a null check, so an NPE occurs during token issuance if the provider is not registered.
OAuth2GrantType.Context captures grantType from formParams once at construction. setFormParams() does not refresh it, so getGrantType() can return stale data.

getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory as an abstract method with no default. Custom grant factories compiled against the old interface throw AbstractMethodError in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit.

Token ID decoding requires an exact 6-character 2+2+2 prefix. However, the getShortcut() javadoc says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, and nothing validates that shortcuts are 2 characters. Custom grants with 3-letter shortcuts therefore produce IDs that getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects.
The new unit test calls org.junit.Assert.assertEquals with the actual and expected arguments swapped, contrary to docs/tests-development.md.
An outdated comment saying 'starts at 4th char' is left over from the earlier 3-letter encoding.
The commit format breaches CONTRIBUTING.md: there are two commits instead of one, ee2491268a uses lowercase 'closes #37118', and daffb05b5a has no issue link.
grantsToShortcuts duplicates sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, gt) with a hand-maintained, unsynchronised cache that can go stale on undeploy.

The lazy/hot-deploy refresh paths in getGrantTypeByShortcut (lines 106-137) add entries without the duplicate-shortcut check that postInit performs, so a custom grant can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping.
The access-token jti and event token_id format changes from a bare UUID to '<ss><tt><gg>:<uuid>' with no upgrade/release note, as required by PR-CHECKLIST.md.
The @Column(name='ID', length = 36) annotation is shorter than the new 43-character access-token IDs.
The shortcut maps include UNKNOWN 'un' entries, so decode accepts IDs like 'ununna:x' that encodeTokenId refuses to encode.
The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed from the grant SPI.
A null return from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() causes an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put in postInit.

Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a pure alias of OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, and the patch uses both inconsistently: OAuth2GrantType.Context reads OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, while grants and TokenManager write Constants.GRANT_TYPE.
